cards.front: Recall a key point about Precambrian & Early Earth
cards.back: The Precambrian spans from Earth's formation (~4.6 billion years ago) to the start of the Cambrian (~541 million years ago), about 88% of geological time

cards.front: Recall a key point about Precambrian & Early Earth
cards.back: Earth formed from accretion of planetesimals; heavy elements sank to form the core while lighter material formed the mantle and crust

cards.front: Recall a key point about Precambrian & Early Earth
cards.back: The early atmosphere was rich in CO2, water vapour, nitrogen and sulfur compounds; oxygen was absent

cards.front: Recall a key point about Precambrian & Early Earth
cards.back: Stromatolites (layered structures built by cyanobacteria) appear from ~3.5 billion years ago and produced oxygen through photosynthesis

cards.front: Recall a key point about Precambrian & Early Earth
cards.back: The Great Oxidation Event (~2.4 billion years ago) oxygenated the atmosphere, enabled banded iron formations and allowed complex life to evolve

cards.front: Recall a key point about Precambrian & Early Earth
cards.back: Banded iron formations (BIFs) formed when dissolved iron in the oceans reacted with oxygen, precipitating iron oxide layers
